LESSON: POPULATION GROWTH IN AFRICA

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Relationships
Topic 3.4: Population Growth in Africa

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Population Growth in Africa
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why is it important to study demographic changes?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. create awareness on the effects of population growth in the community
2. appreciate the impact of migration on population growth in Africa

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Skill 1: create awareness on the effects of population growth in the community

Teach
• Today’s focus: create awareness on the effects of population growth in the community.
• Listen/read the idea.
• Watch/study the model.
• Then do Try this.

• Model B for “create awareness on the effects of population growth in the community” using a home/county example.

Try this

• Share with a partner and improve one bullet.

▸ Skill 2: appreciate the impact of migration on population growth in Africa

• Today’s focus: appreciate the impact of migration on population growth in Africa.
• Listen/read the idea.
• Watch/study the model.
• Then do Try this.

• Share with a partner and improve one bullet.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• Model 1: create awareness on the effects of population growth in the community
• Model 2: appreciate the impact of migration on population growth in Africa

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Practise: create awareness on the effects of population growth in the community
2. Practise: appreciate the impact of migration on population growth in Africa

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Make a one-page revision sheet for Population Growth in Africa.
2. Teach someone at home for 2 minutes using bullet points only.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to study demographic changes?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• create awareness on the effects of population growth in the community
• appreciate the impact of migration on population growth in Africa

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
